candidates.title: Evaluate complete procedural outputs alongside partial progress
candidates.rule: For agents following long manuals, score the complete required result and omissions separately from retrieved-snippet relevance or partial-answer overlap.
candidates.passage: exact match stays at 1% or below across all baselines
candidates.finding: In TAM, code-set overlap and locally plausible steps coexist with very low complete-output accuracy. Failure traces include wrong anchors, incomplete execution and missing elements. The evaluation recommendation is inferred from these gaps.
models: GPT-5 used in described RAG baseline; other baseline models not fully established in inspected sections
candidates.conditions: Baselines share case inputs and manual sources but differ in access and orchestration. The failure sample deliberately selects fifty non-exact cases.
candidates.limitations: Exact-match targets can have annotation ambiguity. Provider filtering causes thirty-five harness cases to return no answer, confounding comparisons. This is a benchmark finding, not clinical or legal guidance or a validated deployment solution.
candidates.validation_test: On a representative manual task, define complete-output checks and partial diagnostics before comparing harnesses. Record missing requirements, wrong anchors, abstentions and provider failures separately.
